## 1. Project Description
Ledger is a native Android application for students, roommates, and friends who need personal expense records and shared-expense coordination. Personal Account Management supports manual entry, statement import, receipt recognition, duplicate review, historical currency conversion, and manual cloud saves. Expense Group Management supports invitations, membership management, shared expenses with several split methods, and live updates. With Let's Go Dutch, signed-in users can copy a personal expense into a group to split it with other members. They can also save their own share of a group expense as a new entry in their personal spending ledger.

Personal records are kept on the device. Signed-in users can manually save their ledger to one of three cloud slots or restore a saved copy to replace their device ledger. They can also copy a personal expense into a group or record their share of a group expense in their personal ledger. These are one-time copies: changes made later do not carry over, and cloud saves do not automatically sync or merge records.

## 2. Requirements Specification

### 2.1. Features and Current Scope

| Feature | Implemented scope | Planned extension |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Authentication and Account Management** — supporting functionality | Username/password and Google registration and sign-in; explicit linking of Google to an existing account; viewing and editing the profile (display name, cropped profile photo, password); revocable sessions; sign-out. | Per-account quotas for paid document recognition. |
| **Feature 1 — Personal Account Management** | Local income/expense entry, editing and deletion; CSV import on Android; supported text-PDF statement parsing on the backend; optional OpenAI receipt/statement recognition for signed-in users; editable import review; duplicate suggestions; historical FX quotes and local conversion; three named manual whole-ledger cloud save slots per account. | Automatic cloud synchronization and merging edits from several devices. |
| **Feature 2 — Expense Group Management** | Create and list groups; generate, preview, and accept invitations; rename groups; leave a group; owner removal of members and group deletion; create, edit, and delete shared expenses, entered by hand or from a receipt photo or file through **Add a bill**; tax and tip on every split; Equal, Percentage, and Custom amounts (with an optional meal calculator for GST, extra tax and tip); spending totals and allocated shares; live updates when members or expenses change; sharing a personal expense to groups and importing one's own share (UC-03). | Repayments and net balances, group currency conversion, and settlement-based archival. |
| **Feature 3 — Let's Go Dutch** | Start a split session from a reviewed itemized receipt, typed or recognized through **Add a bill**; claim and release item units; tax and tip shared in proportion to claimed items; live allocation updates; reconnect recovery; owner finalization into one group expense. | None. |

Personal Account Management and expense groups support CAD, USD, EUR, GBP, CNY, JPY, AUD, HKD, SGD, KRW, MXN, and INR. They also support multiple language, including English, Chinese, French.

### 2.3. Actors

| Actor | Responsibility and access |
| --- | --- |
| **User** | A person using Ledger, with or without an account can use the installation-local Personal Account Management feature and choose to register or sign in. |
| **Authenticated User** | A user with a valid Ledger account, can view and edit account information, use cloud saves and document recognition, create/list their groups, and preview or accept an invitation. |
| **Group Member** | An Authenticated User included in an active group can view its expenses, create expenses, share a personal expense to the group, import their own share, generate invitations, rename the group, leave the group, and claim or release receipt items in a split session. They can edit or delete a shared expense they created. |
| **Group Owner** | Group owner can remove members, delete the group, edit or delete any expense in it, and start and finalize split sessions. Leaving as the owner deletes the group.|
| **Google Authentication** | Provides Google identity evidence verified by User Management. Ledger issues its own session after verification. |
| **OpenAI Document Recognition** | Extracts transaction suggestions from explicitly submitted images/PDFs. Current receipt extraction returns a transaction for the receipt total, not claimable item units; split-session items are entered manually. |
| **Exchange-rate Service (Frankfurter / ECB)** | Supplies historical exchange-rate quotes. Expense Management uses those quotes to calculate reporting-currency amounts on Android. |

### 2.4. Use Case Descriptions

#### Authentication and Account Management — Supporting Functionality

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Sign In** | Sign in with a Ledger username and password, or with Google. The app then returns to My Expenses, or continues an invitation that was waiting for sign-in. |
| **Register an Account** | Create an account with a username (3–30 letters, digits, dots, hyphens or underscores) and a password of 8–128 characters, entered twice. A first-time Google user either sets a username and password for a new account, or links an existing Ledger account by entering its username and password. Each username and Google identity can belong to only one account. |
| **Edit Account Information** | Change the profile photo (take or choose a picture, then crop it), the display name, the optional email and phone number, and the password. Changing the email or password needs the current password, or a Google confirmation for an account without one, and signs out the user's other devices. |
| **Sign Out** | Log out from Me. If the device holds personal records, the app first asks whether to save them to a cloud slot or delete them from the device. The local session is cleared and the server session is revoked; if the network is unavailable, the server session simply expires. |

#### Feature 1 — Personal Account Management

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Import a Receipt (UC-01)** | While signed in, choose **Add a bill**, then take a receipt photo or choose an image or PDF. Images are compressed on the device to 5 MiB; PDFs can be up to 20 MB. The backend sends the document to OpenAI Document Recognition, which returns the transaction and, for a single receipt, its items, tax and tip. The user checks and corrects the result before anything is saved: a personal bill is saved to the device after confirmation, and a group bill opens the group expense form with the receipt filled in. |
| **Import a Bank Statement (UC-F1-03)** | Choose a CSV file, which is parsed on the device, or a text PDF from a supported bank, which the backend parses without AI and checks against the statement totals. OpenAI extraction is available as an explicit alternative. Up to 200 rows appear for review; only the selected, valid rows are saved. |
| **Manually Add an Entry (UC-F1-04)** | Enter an income or expense with amount, currency, date, merchant, category and optional notes. The form points out invalid fields, and the entry is saved on the device. |
| **Edit Personal Records** | Open a record to change or delete it, or select several and delete them together after confirmation. A revision check stops an edit from overwriting a newer version. A record already shared to a group is a separate copy, so later edits do not reach the group. |
| **Resolve Duplicate Candidates (UC-02)** | Extends **Import a Bank Statement** and **Import a Receipt**. A row that matches an existing record or another row in the same import is marked as a possible duplicate, with the matching amount, date and merchant shown. The user skips the row or chooses to keep it anyway; the import cannot be confirmed until every flagged row is decided. |
| **Convert Currency (UC-F1-06)** | Choose a reporting currency. Each record is converted with the latest Frankfurter (ECB) rate on or before its date, and keeps its original amount, the rate, the rate date and the source. Saved rates keep working offline. |
| **Save a Cloud Backup (UC-F1-07)** | A signed-in user saves the whole device ledger to one of three named cloud slots, and can rename, overwrite or delete a save. Each save has a revision, so two devices cannot silently overwrite the same slot. |
| **Load a Cloud Backup** | Choose a save and confirm to replace the ledger on this device with it. Records not saved to the cloud are lost; the save itself stays in the account. |

#### Feature 2 — Expense Group Management

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Create an Expense Group** | A signed-in user enters a group name, an optional description and the group currency. The creator becomes the owner and first member, and gets an invitation link right away. |
| **Invite a Group Member** | Any Group Member creates an invitation link, valid for 7 days, and shares or copies it. |
| **Join an Expense Group** | A signed-in user opens an invitation link, or pastes it into **Join group**, sees the group and who sent the invitation, and accepts or rejects it. Accepting again changes nothing. A group holds up to 100 members. |
| **Rename an Expense Group** | Any Group Member renames the group in Group settings. |
| **Record a Group Expense** | A Group Member adds a bill through **Add a bill**, either typed in or filled from a receipt. They enter the description, total in the group currency, optional tax and tip, payer, participants and split method. The backend calculates and stores each share in whole cents. |
| **Edit a Group Expense** | The bill's creator or the Group Owner edits it. The edit must start from the saved version; an unchanged edit writes nothing. If someone in the split has left the group, only the description can change unless the split is entered again for current members. Bills posted by Let's Go Dutch cannot be edited. |
| **Choose a Split Method** | Split a bill with Equal split, Custom amounts or Percentage; every method accepts tax and tip. With Custom amounts, members can enter pretax amounts and share the tax and tip in proportion. The **Let's Go Dutch** button hands the bill over for an itemized split. |
| **Reuse a Personal Bill (UC-03)** | Select personal expenses, choose **Share to groups** and pick groups in the same currency. Each group gets a one-time copy paid by the sharer and split equally among its current members, with the date, category and notes. Each member can then choose **Import my share** to save their allocated share as a personal expense; for the sharer, the original record is updated to that share so the expense is not counted twice. |
| **Leave an Expense Group** | A Group Member leaves a group and loses access to it immediately. Their shares in saved expenses are kept. If the owner leaves, the group is deleted for everyone. |
| **Delete a Group Member** | The Group Owner deletes a member from the group. The member loses access immediately, their shares in saved expenses are kept, and invitations they created stop working. |

#### Feature 3 — Let's Go Dutch

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Start a Split Session** | From the bill form, the Group Owner chooses **Let's Go Dutch**, checks or enters each item's name, quantity (1–20) and unit price, the tax, the tip and the payer, and confirms that they add up to the total. Receipt recognition fills these in when a receipt was used. Each unit, up to 200, can be claimed separately. |
| **Claim Receipt Items (UC-04)** | A Group Member claims an available unit, and can release a unit they claimed. Each unit has at most one owner, and every change appears on the other members' screens right away. |
| **View Live Allocations and Totals** | Every member sees how much is assigned and unassigned, how many units are claimed, the subtotal, tax and tip, and each member's running total with their share of tax and tip. The figures update live and are reloaded after a reconnect. |

### 2.5. Formal Use Case Specifications

#### UC-01 — Import and Review a Receipt

**Status:** Implemented, subject to backend OpenAI configuration and availability.

**Primary actor:** User.

**Preconditions:** The user is signed in, has a readable receipt image or PDF, and can reach the configured backend.

**Postcondition:** The candidate transactions are editable with warnings shown. No personal transaction has been saved; UC-02 covers confirmation and commit.

**Main success scenario**

1. The user opens **+ Add a bill** from My Expenses or a group, chooses who the bill is for, and selects a supported receipt image or PDF through the Android document picker (camera capture is an alternative for images).
2. The app explains the external processing and the user chooses **Send to OpenAI & extract**.
3. Expense Management validates the selection, compresses an image larger than 5 MiB, and sends `fileName`, `mimeType`, `dataBase64`, and `defaultCurrency` with the Ledger session to `POST /api/ledger/imports/preview`.
4. User Management checks the session before the upload is parsed. Bill Import validates the file and resource limits, then calls OpenAI Document Recognition through `OpenAiDocumentExtractor`.
5. The service returns transaction candidates and warnings. A single receipt has one candidate for its total, including tax/tip, and `receipt` holds its subtotal, tax, tip and items.
6. Expense Management validates the candidate structure and displays editable amount, currency, date, merchant, kind, category, and notes. The user corrects missing or inaccurate values.
7. Expense Management checks the edited rows and computes duplicate suggestions against the local ledger and selected import rows.
8. The app stays in import review for selection, duplicate acknowledgement, and the explicit save action in UC-02.

**Failure scenarios**

- **2a — Cancellation:** No extraction request is sent before confirmation; canceling review saves no transaction.
- **3a/4a — Invalid file:** Empty/invalid data or an invalid name is rejected; unsupported content/type yields 415, and excessive size may yield 400 or 413 depending on the failed validation. Images are limited to 5 MiB after on-device compression and PDFs to 20 MiB.
- **4c — Missing or expired session:** Return 401 before the upload is read; the app asks the user to sign in again.
- **4b — Service unavailable:** Missing configuration, timeout, or upstream failure shows an error and permits retry/manual entry. Rate limits return 429; exhausted extraction capacity returns 503.
- **5b — Bill for a group:** A single receipt opens that group's expense form filled in from `receipt`, where the user chooses the split or **Let's Go Dutch**, and nothing is saved until they confirm. A currency different from the group's is flagged and not converted. A statement with several rows stays in My Expenses.
- **5a — Invalid or empty extraction:** Show the returned warning/error and request a clearer document or manual entry. Missing financial values are not invented.
- **6a/7a — Invalid fields or duplicate suggestions:** Keep the rows in review. Invalid selected rows and unacknowledged duplicate candidates cannot be committed.

#### UC-02 — Resolve Duplicate Candidates

**Status:** Implemented.

**Primary actor:** User.

**Preconditions:** A receipt/statement/CSV import preview exists in the Android app. Existing records are scoped to the current installation.

**Postcondition:** Selected valid rows and their request result are committed atomically to SQLite, or no selected row is inserted.

**Main success scenario**

1. Expense Management loads existing local records and reviews the current import rows using `LedgerDomain.review`.
2. The app shows duplicate candidates with matching amount, date, and merchant evidence. Scores are heuristic indicators, not probabilities.
3. The user skips rows they do not want and acknowledges any duplicate candidates they choose to keep.
4. The app calls `LedgerRepository.commitImport(rows, source, fileName, requestId)` with the current selections and acknowledgements.
5. Expense Management checks the persisted request fingerprint. A matching completed request returns its saved count; a new request is revalidated against the current local records and selected batch.
6. Expense Management obtains any required historical quote from its cache or Bill Import, computes converted minor units locally, and validates totals before inserting records.
7. One SQLite transaction inserts all accepted records and the request result. The backend stores neither the records nor the import result.
8. The app reports the number imported and returns to the local transaction list.

**Failure scenarios**

- **2a — No matches:** No duplicate acknowledgement is required; normal field validation and explicit confirmation still apply.
- **3a — A separate purchase resembles an existing one:** The user can keep both; suggestions never force a merge.
- **5a — Reused request ID with changed content:** Reject it locally. This is a `LedgerException`, not an HTTP 409 from a personal-transaction API.
- **5b — Current records reveal an unacknowledged duplicate or invalid row:** Stop before inserting; retain the review for correction.
- **6a — Required FX unavailable:** Save no selected records; keep the draft available for retry.
- **7a — SQLite failure:** Roll back the entire record/request transaction. A retry of an already committed identical request returns its original result without reinserting records.

Manual entry uses local field validation and saves through `LedgerRepository.save`. The current manual-entry editor does not suggest duplicates or request duplicate acknowledgement; those controls belong to import review.

#### UC-F1-03 — Import a Bank Statement

**Primary actor:** User. **Preconditions:** My Expenses is open; a readable CSV or supported USD Chase/American Express text PDF is available. **Postcondition:** A review exists, or the previous ledger is unchanged; only UC-02 commits records.

**Main success scenario**

1. The user opens **+ Add a bill**, chooses a file in Android DocumentsUI and returns to Ledger.
2. For CSV, the user chooses **Preview CSV**; Android parses the required date, amount and merchant/description columns. For PDF, the user chooses **Preview statement**; Bill Import reads the actual PDF and reconciles details against statement totals without AI.
3. The app displays editable rows and warnings; refunds are income with a warning, card repayments are excluded, and foreign-spend notes retain the billed USD amount as the ledger amount.
4. The user corrects invalid fields and continues through UC-02 to select, acknowledge duplicates and commit.

**Alternate and failure scenarios**

- **1a — Picker canceled:** Return to Import without a selected file or a write.
- **1b — Empty/unreadable selection:** Show an error and save nothing.
- **2a — Malformed CSV:** Missing required columns or invalid syntax prevents preview. Invalid row values remain editable and prevent confirmation while selected.
- **2b — Unsupported/damaged PDF or unreconciled totals:** Show the backend error (415/422); never show a partial successful statement or silently send it to AI. The user can choose a different file or explicitly use UC-01.
- **3a — Abandon review:** **Start a different import** asks for confirmation; **Keep reviewing** preserves it and **Discard review** removes it without a write.
- **2c — Backend/network unavailable:** Keep the selected document available for retry; save nothing.

#### UC-F1-04 — Manually Add an Entry

**Primary actor:** User. **Precondition:** My Expenses is open. **Postcondition:** Exactly one valid local transaction is saved, or the ledger is unchanged.

**Main success scenario**

1. Choose **+ Add a bill**, keep **Just me**, choose **Enter manually**, and enter amount, original currency, date, merchant, kind, category and optional notes.
2. Choose **Save transaction**. The app validates the fields.
3. Expense Management obtains any necessary historical FX quote and saves the record with an operation key in SQLite.
4. The dashboard shows the record and updated totals; activity recreation retains it.

**Alternate and failure scenarios**

- **2a — Invalid fields:** Show **Check transaction**, preserve the draft and save nothing; correct and retry.
- **1a — Leave a changed draft:** Confirm discarding or continue editing; activity recreation preserves an unsaved draft.
- **3a — Required FX or SQLite write fails:** Show the error, preserve the draft and save no partial record.

#### UC-F1-05 — Review and Edit Personal Records

**Primary actor:** User. **Precondition:** The local ledger contains records. **Postcondition:** Only explicitly confirmed records are changed/deleted; totals reflect the visible filters.

**Main success scenario**

1. Browse My Expenses, choose a month/kind filter or search merchant/category/notes; read the resulting records and totals.
2. Open a record, edit its fields and choose **Save transaction**; the revision-checked write updates that record.
3. For single deletion, open the record and confirm **Delete transaction**. For batch deletion, choose **Select transactions**, select individual records or **Select all shown**, then confirm **Delete selected**.
4. Read the remaining records and updated totals; reopen the activity to verify persistence.

**Alternate and failure scenarios**

- **2a — Invalid edit:** Validation prevents a write and keeps the editor available.
- **3a — Cancellation:** **Keep transaction** or batch **Cancel** preserves every selected record.
- **3b — Filters change during selection:** Clear selection so hidden records cannot be deleted accidentally.
- **2b/3c — Stale revision or SQLite failure:** Reject stale changes; a failed batch rolls back all selected deletions.

#### UC-F1-06 — Convert Reporting Currency

**Primary actor:** User. **Precondition:** A personal ledger exists. **Postcondition:** Reporting currency and all converted values change together; original currency/amount/date remain intact.

**Main success scenario**

1. Choose another currency from the dashboard currency menu.
2. Expense Management obtains historical quotes from its local cache or `GET /api/ledger/exchange` for each original currency/date.
3. Preserve the actual effective rate date (a weekend can use Friday), rate and source; calculate rounded reporting minor units locally.
4. Atomically update the reporting currency and records, then display recalculated summaries.

**Failure scenarios**

- **2a — FX unavailable/invalid:** Show an error and retain the previous currency and every record; retry when available.
- **4a — Persistence failure:** Roll back all revaluations and the preference change.

#### UC-F1-07 — Save and Load Cloud Saves

**Primary actor:** Authenticated User. **Preconditions:** Valid session; backend reachable. A free slot is needed for a new save. **Postcondition:** An explicitly named whole-ledger snapshot is stored, restored or deleted; no automatic merge occurs.

**Main success scenario**

1. Open **Me → Cloud saves** and read the account's three slots.
2. Select **Save** in a slot, enter a name and confirm; the backend stores the whole device ledger snapshot and a revision.
3. Choose **Rename**, enter another name and save; the slot retains its snapshot.
4. Choose **Load**, review the replacement warning and confirm; validate the snapshot and atomically replace the device ledger, including reporting currency.
5. Choose **Delete** and confirm to remove the server slot; device records remain.

**Alternate and failure scenarios**

- **2a/4a/5a — Cancel:** Close the dialog without uploading, restoring or deleting.
- **1a — Missing/expired session:** Require sign-in; do not expose another account's saves.
- **2b/3a/5b — Stale slot revision:** Reject with 409 and refresh rather than overwriting silently.
- **4b — Invalid snapshot/local write failure:** Preserve the current ledger; do not partially restore.
- **1b–5c — Backend/network failure:** Show the failure and allow retry; a failed load leaves device records intact.

These specifications describe product behavior. [Testing.md](Testing.md) records which scenarios have actual UI E2E evidence and which currently have only interface/integration evidence; specifying a scenario does not claim it has passed.

#### UC-03 — Reuse and Split a Personal Bill

**Status:** Implemented.

**Primary actor:** Group Member, Group Owner.

**Preconditions:** The user has a valid session and belongs to at least one active group.

**Postcondition:** Each selected group holds one independent copy of each selected expense, split equally among its current members with the sharer as payer. Later edits to the personal record do not change the group expense.

**Main success scenario**

1. In **My Expenses**, the member chooses **Share to groups** on an expense. Expense Management reads the records from SQLite; the backend never looks up personal records.
2. The app lists the member's groups and enables only those whose currency matches every selected record. 
3. The member selects one or more groups.
4. The app shows the fields that will become visible to group members (amount, date, merchant, category and notes), and the member chooses **Share selected**.
5. For each group, the app sends `{sourceId, input}` to `POST /api/groups/{groupId}/shared-entries`.
6. User Management authenticates the caller. Group Bill Splitting checks active membership and validates the expense input.
7. Group Bill Splitting splits the amount equally among the current members in integer cents and saves the expense with the caller as payer and creator.
8. The backend publishes `onGroupChanged`, so other members' open group pages refresh. The app shows the progress for each group and reports success.
9. Later, any member can choose **Import my share** on a group expense. After the import the button is disabled and reads **Imported** for that member, on every device.

**Failure scenarios**

- **2a — No eligible group:** The dialog explains that the member must create or join a group with the same currency; nothing is sent. Income cannot be shared.
- **3a — The member cancels:** Nothing is sent and no group expense is saved.
- **5a — Expired session or lost membership:** Return 401 or 404 for that group; the member signs in again or chooses another group.
- **6a — Lost response:** Retrying the same source record and content returns the existing expense with `alreadyShared: true` instead of creating a duplicate.
- **6b — Changed original shared again:** Return 409 and direct the member to edit the saved group expense.
- **7a — One group fails:** Copies already saved in other groups remain; a retry submits only the unfinished groups. Sharing across several groups is not one atomic transaction.
- **8a — Allocation changed before confirmation:** The app fetches the allocation again before writing and asks the member to review it.
- **8b — Repeated import:** The saved import receipt makes a repeat a no-op. If the share would replace the member's own original record on this installation, the app warns before replacing it.

#### UC-04 — Claim or Unclaim Receipt Items Live

**Status:** Implemented.

**Primary actor:** Group Member.

**Preconditions:** The member belongs to an active group with a split session.

**Postcondition:** An accepted claim/release changes one unit's owner and its derived allocations exactly once; subscribers receive the committed state.

**Main success scenario**

1. The member opens **Claim items** in the group, shown while a split is open, and sees available units, owners, and totals.
2. The member selects **Claim** on an available unit or **Release** on their own unit.
3. The app stores the operation key and payload in private pending storage, marks the action pending, and sends `unitId`, `action`, `version`, and `operationKey` to `POST /api/split-sessions/{sessionId}/claims`.
4. Group Bill Splitting uses User Management to authenticate the caller, then verifies membership, session status, and expected version.
5. A conditional single-document update assigns/releases the unit. Only one conflicting claimant can succeed.
6. The same update advances the version and sequence and appends the event and operation result.
7. After the write, the backend returns `{session, operation}` to the caller and publishes **`onGroupUpdated`** to the group's subscribers, rechecking each subscriber's session and membership.
8. Apps apply each event once in sequence order, replace the pending state with the committed allocations, and clear the stored operation key.

**Failure scenarios**

- **4a — Finalized session or lost membership:** Return 409 for a closed session or 404 for a former member; the app refreshes or leaves the session.
- **5a — Taken unit or stale version:** Return 409 with current state and undo the pending preview.
- **5b — Releasing another member's unit:** Return 403 and make no change.
- **6a — Lost acknowledgement:** Resolve/retry the same operation key and payload; do not generate a second operation automatically.
- **8a — Duplicate/out-of-order event:** Ignore duplicates; recover a gap through UC-05 instead of guessing state.

#### UC-05 — Recover Live State After Reconnect

**Status:** Implemented.

**Primary actor:** Group Member.

**Preconditions:** The app knows the group ID, the last applied sequence of each split session, and any pending operation keys.

**Postcondition:** The app installs a consistent snapshot, reconciles pending operations, and resumes ordered live updates.

**Main success scenario**

1. The app detects a disconnection or a sequence gap, shows the session as read-only, and pauses new claims, releases and finalization.
2. The backend rechecks the session and current group membership before joining the group room.
3. The app buffers arriving `onGroupUpdated` events and requests `GET /api/groups/{groupId}/snapshot`.
4. Group Bill Splitting completes any interrupted finalization, then returns `{groupId, expenses, splitSessions}`.
5. The app installs the snapshot, discards buffered events at or below each session's sequence, and applies only contiguous later events.
6. For each pending operation key, the app calls `GET /api/operations/{operationKey}`.
7. The app shows the session as live and enables new claims after recovery.

**Failure scenarios**

- **2a — Expired session:** Require reauthentication before restoring protected live state.
- **2b — Lost membership:** The subscription is rejected; the app discards the inaccessible group state and returns to the group list.
- **3a — Another connection failure:** Keep the view read-only, retry the connection after 1–10 seconds, and refresh the snapshot over REST every 3 seconds in the meantime.
- **5a — Remaining gap or unavailable replay:** Request a fresh snapshot; do not extrapolate allocations or balances.
- **6a — Unresolved operation:** Keep the action labelled pending until lookup/idempotent retry establishes its result.

### 2.6. Non-Functional Requirements

| Requirement | Target and rationale | Current boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **NFR-1 — Financial Integrity** | Accepted shares must sum exactly to the expense total, and retries must not duplicate a saved financial operation. Item claims must have at most one owner per unit.| Integer arithmetic for every split mode, deterministic remainders, exact custom sums, request deduplication, edit/delete revisions, exclusive unit ownership with versioned claims, operation keys, and recoverable finalization are implemented. Settlement invariants remain planned with repayments. |
| **NFR-2 — Access Control and Privacy** | Every protected request/subscription must verify identity and ownership/membership. Release traffic must use HTTPS and live traffic WSS. Recognition requires explicit submission. | Account, group, split-session, cloud-save, and paid recognition routes require a session; group routes and live subscriptions also check membership. Personal records are installation-local. Exchange-rate, metadata, and text-PDF statement routes remain guest routes with rate limits. “Every protected path” is a design obligation, not a claim of measured 100% test coverage. |
| **NFR-3 — Real-Time Responsiveness** | In a split session at the backend's limits (100 group members, 200 item units), at least 95% of accepted claims and releases should appear on the other members' screens within 1 second. A member whose connection drops should see the current server state within 5 seconds after the network returns.<br><br>**Why these numbers:** 100 members and 200 units are the largest group and session the backend accepts, so the target covers every case the app allows. 1 second is the longest delay that keeps the user's flow of thought uninterrupted, even though the delay is noticed (Nielsen, *Usability Engineering*, 1993). Members claim items at the same table, so a slower update invites two people to tap the same item. 95% rather than every update, because mobile networks occasionally delay a message; a late update never produces a wrong result, since the backend accepts only one owner per unit and the recovery path repairs the screen. A dropped connection is shown on screen and pauses claims, so recovery must finish well inside the 10 seconds a user keeps attention on a waiting task (same source); 5 seconds leaves half of that as margin. The app meets it with a 3-second snapshot poll plus up to 2 seconds for that request over a mobile connection (Section 3.8). | Live delivery and recovery are implemented. These targets have not yet been measured at the stated load. |

## 3. Design Specification

### 3.1. Domain Components and Responsibility Boundaries

Ledger’s backend is deployed as a single Express/TypeScript application organized into four logical components: User Management, Group and Invitation Management, Group Bill Splitting, and Bill Import. The diagrams use these component names and refer to the personal accounting domain as Expense Management, which runs on the Android front end.

#### User Management

- Handles account registration, password and Google sign-in, identity linking, profile updates, Ledger sessions, and up to three named cloud saves per account. Keeping authentication and session management here lets other components reuse the same identity checks, while account-level cloud saves stay separate from the working ledger on Android.

#### Group and Invitation Management

- Create active groups; manage names, membership, invitation generation/preview/acceptance, member departure, removal, and deletion. This method ensures that joining, leaving, and removing members follow consistent rules.


#### Group Bill Splitting

- Validate and create/edit/delete shared expenses; compute Equal, Percentage and Custom splits. Keeping split calculations and expense updates in one component ensures that the same rules apply whether a shared expense is entered manually or copied from a personal record.

#### Bill Import

- Bill Import validates uploaded files, parses supported text-based PDF statements, uses OpenAI to suggest transactions for user review, and retrieves and validates historical exchange rates from Frankfurter (ECB data). Keeping file parsing and external API calls here lets Expense Management focus on reviewing and saving transactions.

### 3.2. Databases and State Ownership

#### MongoDB — Backend Account and Group State
It stores the working personal ledger on the device. Local storage lets users record and review expenses offline without signing in.

#### SQLite — Android Expense Management
Android SQLite stores the working personal ledger on the device so users can record and review expenses offline. Restoring a cloud save replaces the local ledger in a single transaction after validation, without merging it with existing records.

### 3.3. External Modules

| Module | Current interface and purpose | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Google Authentication** | `verifyGoogleToken(idToken, audience)` uses `google-auth-library` to verify Google tokens and obtain verified identity evidence. | Used by User Management; Ledger issues its own session rather than using the Google token as a group API session. |
| **OpenAI Document Recognition** | `OpenAiDocumentExtractor.extract(file, defaultCurrency): Promise<Extraction>` calls the Responses API with structured transaction output. | Used by Bill Import after explicit submission by a signed-in user. Requires backend-only configuration. Current receipt output is a transaction total, not an itemized claiming model. |
| **Exchange-rate Service (Frankfurter / ECB)** | `FrankfurterFxProvider.quote(from, to, date): Promise<ExchangeQuote>` requests historical rates from Frankfurter. | Implemented. Returns `{rate, date, source}`; Expense Management performs amount conversion. A prior effective date is accepted only within the configured seven-day tolerance. |
| **PDF.js (`pdfjs-dist`)** | `extractStatement(file)` parses supported text-PDF statement layouts and checks reconciliation within Ledger's backend process. | Implemented for supported Chase/Amex layouts. No external AI request; this is not offline Android PDF parsing or universal PDF/OCR support. |

### 3.4. Main Interfaces

#### Conventions

All `/api/groups/*`, `/api/split-sessions/*`, `/api/operations/*` and `/api/ledger-saves/*` routes, profile retrieval and update, logout, and `POST /api/ledger/imports/preview` require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The other `/api/ledger/*` routes are guest routes. API errors return `{error}`; Expense Management errors are local exceptions.

`Session` is `{token, expiresAt, user}`. `ExchangeQuote` is `{rate, date, source}`, with the rate as decimal text. `Extraction` is `{candidates: [{rowId, input, warnings}], warnings}`, where `input` has `kind`, `amount`, `currency`, `date`, `merchant`, `category` and `notes`.

#### User Management — HTTP Interfaces

| Interface | Input | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/auth/register` | `username, password, confirmPassword` | 201 `Session`; creates a password account. |
| `POST /api/auth/login` | `username, password` | 200 `Session`. |
| `POST /api/auth/google` | `idToken` | 200 `{status: "signed-in", ...Session}` or `{status: "registration-required", profile}`. |
| `POST /api/auth/google/register` | `idToken, username, password, confirmPassword` | 201 session for a new account; 200 for an existing Google identity. |
| `POST /api/auth/google/link` | `idToken, username, password` | 200 session; links the Google identity to an existing password account. |
| `GET /api/users/me` | Session | 200 `{user}`. |
| `PATCH /api/users/me` | `displayName?`, `avatarDataUrl?`, `newPassword?`, plus `currentPassword` or `googleIdToken` for a password change | 200 `{user}`; a wrong current password returns 403. |
| `POST /api/auth/logout` | Session | 204; revokes the session. |
| `GET /api/ledger-saves` | Session | 200 `{slots}`; summaries of the three slots. |
| `GET /api/ledger-saves/{slot}` | Slot 1–3 | 200 `{save}` with records; 404 if empty. |
| `PUT /api/ledger-saves/{slot}` | `name, deviceName, baseCurrency, records, replaces` | 200 `{save}`. `replaces` is the revision being overwritten, or `null` for an empty slot; a mismatch returns 409. |
| `PATCH /api/ledger-saves/{slot}` | `name, revision` | 200 `{save}`; renames without re-uploading. |
| `DELETE /api/ledger-saves/{slot}?revision=` | Slot and revision | 204; device records are unaffected. |

Invalid credentials or sessions return 401, invalid registration fields 400, and conflicting identities 409.

#### Group and Invitation Management — HTTP Interfaces

| Interface | Input | Result and permission |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/groups` | `name, description?, currency?, requestId` | 201 `{group, invitation}`; any Authenticated User. Default currency CAD; a matching retry returns 200 and may create a new invitation. |
| `GET /api/groups` | Session | 200 `{groups}`; the caller's active groups. |
| `POST /api/groups/{groupId}/invitations` | Group ID | 201 `{invitation}` with link, token and expiry; any member. |
| `GET /api/groups/invitations/{token}` | Token | 200 `{group, inviterName, expiresAt, alreadyMember}`; preview without joining. |
| `POST /api/groups/invitations/{token}/accept` | Token | 200 `{group}`; adds the caller once, within the member limit. |
| `PUT /api/groups/{groupId}/name` | `name` | 200 `{group}`; any member. |
| `DELETE /api/groups/{groupId}` | Group ID | 204; owner only, soft deletion. |
| `POST /api/groups/{groupId}/leave` | Group ID | 204; the group is deleted if the caller is the owner. |
| `DELETE /api/groups/{groupId}/members/{memberId}` | Group and member IDs | 204; owner only, and not the owner themself. |
| `GET /invite/{token}` | Token; public | HTML fallback with group and inviter names and a link into the app; grants no access. |
| `GET /.well-known/assetlinks.json` | Public | Android App Link association; no user data. |

#### Group Bill Splitting — HTTP Interfaces

| Interface | Input | Result and permission |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/groups/{groupId}/expenses` | `description, amount, paidBy, splitMode, shares[], requestId` | 201 `{expense}`, or 200 for an identical retry; any member. |
| `PUT /api/groups/{groupId}/expenses/{expenseId}` | `description, amount, paidBy, splitMode, shares[], revision` | 200 `{expense}`; creator or owner. A stale revision or a split-session expense returns 409. |
| `DELETE /api/groups/{groupId}/expenses/{expenseId}?revision=` | Expense ID and revision | 204; creator or owner. A stale revision or a split-session expense returns 409. |
| `GET /api/groups/{groupId}/summary` | Group ID | 200 `{group, totalCents, expenseCount, memberShares, expenses, recentLimit}`; members only. Includes member names and roles, and `canEdit` and the caller's `importedByMe` per expense. |
| `POST /api/groups/{groupId}/shared-entries` | `sourceId, input` (personal transaction) | 201 `{expense, alreadyShared: false}`, or 200 with `alreadyShared: true` for a repeat; equal split with the caller as payer. A changed repeat returns 409. |
| `GET /api/groups/{groupId}/expenses/{expenseId}/personal-entry` | Expense ID | 200 `{input, groupName, expenseId, sourcePersonalId, importedByMe}` with only the caller's positive share. |
| `POST /api/groups/{groupId}/expenses/{expenseId}/personal-entry/imported` | Expense ID | 200 `{importedByMe: true}`, also on repeat; the caller needs a positive share. Records the caller's import without changing the expense revision. |
| `POST /api/groups/{groupId}/split-sessions` | `reviewed, requestId, description, amountCents, taxCents?, tipCents?, paidBy, units[]` | 201 `{session}`, or 200 for an identical retry; owner only. 1–200 positive units that, with tax and tip, add up exactly to the total. |
| `POST /api/split-sessions/{sessionId}/claims` | `unitId, action` (`claim` or `unclaim`), `version, operationKey` | 200 `{session, operation}`; 409 for a taken unit, stale version or closed session; 403 for releasing another member's unit. |
| `POST /api/split-sessions/{sessionId}/finalize` | `version, operationKey` | 200 `{session, operation, expense}`; owner only, once every unit is assigned. Posts one expense with its subtotal, tax and tip even when retried. |
| `GET /api/groups/{groupId}/snapshot` | Group ID | 200 `{groupId, expenses, splitSessions}`; completes any interrupted finalization first. |
| `GET /api/operations/{operationKey}` | Operation key | 200 `{operation}`, with `expense` when available; 404 for another member's operation. |

Amounts travel as decimal text. `splitMode` is `equal`, `percentage`, `adjusted` (Equal + adjustments) or `custom`; each share is `{userId, amount?, percentage?, adjustment?}`, and a Custom meal adds `customCalculation {tipRate, members[{userId, subtotal, extraTaxRate}]}`, which the backend recalculates. Stored allocations are `{userId, amountCents}`. Payer and participants must be members; participants are unique and number 1–100. The currency comes from the group. `memberShares` is allocated spending, not debt.

#### Bill Import — HTTP Interfaces

| Interface | Input | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/ledger/meta` | None | 200 `{currencies, categories, documentImportAvailable, localStatementImportAvailable, maxDocumentBytes, maxImageBytes}`. |
| `GET /api/ledger/exchange` | `from, to, date=YYYY-MM-DD` | 200 `ExchangeQuote` for a date from 1999-01-04 to today (UTC); a rate, not a converted amount. |
| `POST /api/ledger/imports/preview` | `fileName, mimeType, dataBase64, defaultCurrency`; session | 200 `Extraction` from OpenAI, with `receipt {subtotal, tax, tip, items[{name, quantity, unitPrice}]}` for a single receipt; no database write. 401 without a valid session. |
| `POST /api/ledger/imports/statement-preview` | Same payload | 200 `Extraction` from the backend text-PDF parser, without AI. |

Images are limited to 5 MiB and PDFs to 20 MiB, and files must have a JPEG, PNG, WebP or PDF signature. The two document routes allow two concurrent extractions in total and have separate rate limits.

#### Internal Component Interfaces

These are code entry points, not public APIs.

| Component | Entry point | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| User Management | `requireSession(users, sessions): RequestHandler` | Verify the token hash, expiry and user, and attach the caller to the request. |
| User Management | `startSession(sessions, user)`; `users.findById(userId)` | Create a session; look up identity and profile data. |
| User Management | `ledgerSavesRouter(users, sessions, store)`; `accountSettingsRouter(users, sessions, verify)` | Cloud-save and profile routes for the signed-in account only. |
| Group and Invitation Management | `groupManagementRouter(users)`; `groupJson(group)` | Group and invitation lifecycle routes and group serialization, behind the parent router's session check. |
| Group Bill Splitting | `groupExpensesRouter(users, sessions)` | Mount the protected group routes (including group management), check membership, create and edit expenses, and build summaries. |
| Group Bill Splitting | `parseMoney(value, allowZero=false): number` | Validate decimal text and convert it to integer cents. |
| Group Bill Splitting | `splitBill(totalCents, mode, input, memberIds, digits): Share[]` | Calculate Equal, Percentage and Equal + adjustments shares, or validate exact Custom amounts. |
| Group Bill Splitting | `calculateMeal(input, memberIds, digits)` | Recalculate a Custom meal, rounding each person's GST, extra tax and pre-tax tip to cents before summing. |
| Group Bill Splitting | `entrySharingRouter()`; `createSplitSessionsRouter(users, sessions)` | Entry-sharing and split-session routes, behind the session and membership checks. |
| Group Bill Splitting | `attachSplitSessionLive(io, users, sessions)` | Authenticate `/dutch` connections, check membership on `subscribe`, and deliver committed events to group rooms. |
| Group and Invitation Management / Group Bill Splitting | `publishMembershipChange(change)`; `publishGroupChange(groupId, type)`; `publishSplitSessionUpdate(session, type, …)` | Announce a committed membership, expense or split-session change to the live publisher. |
| Bill Import | `DocumentExtractor.extract(file, defaultCurrency): Promise<Extraction>` | Return editable candidates via `OpenAiDocumentExtractor` or `extractStatement`. |
| Bill Import | `FxProvider.quote(from, to, date): Promise<ExchangeQuote>` | Return a validated historical quote via `FrankfurterFxProvider`. |
| Expense Management (Android) | `LedgerRepository.previewCsv(text, statementCurrency?)` | Parse CSV rows on the device. |
| Expense Management (Android) | `LedgerRepository.previewDocument(fileName, mimeType, bytes, localOnly=false)` | Validate a document and request backend extraction; `localOnly=true` selects the backend statement parser. |
| Expense Management (Android) | `LedgerRepository.review(rows, existing)` → `LedgerDomain.review` | Validate rows and find duplicates among local records and the import. |
| Expense Management (Android) | `LedgerRepository.commitImport(rows, source, fileName, requestId): Int` | Recheck decisions and quotes, then store the selected records and request result atomically. |
| Expense Management (Android) | `LedgerRepository.save(input, id?, revision?, requestId)`; `setBaseCurrency(currency)` | Save or edit records, or recalculate reporting amounts, with revision and transaction guarantees. |

#### Live Events — Socket.IO `/dutch` Namespace

Connections pass the Ledger session in `auth.token` or the Authorization header; invalid sessions are rejected.

| Event | Direction and payload | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `subscribe` / `unsubscribe` | Client → server, `{groupId}`, acknowledged | Join or leave a group room; joining requires membership. |
| **`onGroupUpdated`** | Server → members, `{groupId, sequence, event, session}` | A committed split-session creation, claim, release or finalization, with the session's sequence for ordering. |
| **`onGroupMembershipChanged`** | Server → members, `{groupId, type}` (`joined`, `left`, `removed`, `deleted`) | Clients reload the group summary; a removed or departing member only receives an access invalidation. |
| **`onGroupChanged`** | Server → members, `{groupId, type}` (`expense-added`, `expense-updated`, `expense-deleted`, `renamed`, `split-finalized`) | Clients reload the group summary and keep unsaved drafts. |

#### Planned Interfaces — Repayments

| Interface | Input | Intended result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/groups/{groupId}/repayments` | `toUserId, amount, operationKey` | A repayment awaiting the recipient's confirmation. |
| `POST /api/repayments/{repaymentId}/confirm` | Repayment ID; recipient's session | The confirmed repayment and recalculated net balances. |

### 3.5. Frameworks and Libraries

| Framework/library | Purpose and reason |
| --- | --- |
| Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Material 3 | Kotlin and Compose build the native Android screens, and Material 3 provides shared controls and styling. Compared with XML layouts and manual view updates, Compose lets the receipt review and live split screens render directly from Kotlin state. Material 3 gives those screens consistent components without a custom widget library. |
| Kotlin coroutines | Coroutines move repository and HTTP work to `Dispatchers.IO` so the UI stays responsive. Compared with callbacks or manually managed threads, suspend functions keep sequential steps, such as importing a receipt and loading its preview, readable at the call site. |
| Android SQLite / `SQLiteOpenHelper` | SQLite stores local entries, cached quotes, preferences, and request replay records. Compared with a preferences store, SQLite supports querying individual entries and committing entries and their request result together. `SQLiteOpenHelper` gives Ledger direct control over its existing SQL and transaction boundaries without adding Room. |
| `HttpURLConnection` and `org.json` | These built-in APIs send REST requests and parse JSON responses. Compared with adding Retrofit and a serializer, they suit Ledger’s approach of sharing HTTP transport logic and mapping payloads explicitly in each feature’s API client. |
| Credential Manager 1.3.0 and googleid 1.1.1 | Credential Manager presents Google account selection, and googleid gives the app the Google ID token to send to the backend. Compared with implementing a browser-based Google OAuth flow directly, this fits Ledger’s native Android sign-in and its existing server-side ID-token verification. |
| Node.js 22 and TypeScript ~5.9 | Node.js runs Ledger’s REST and live-update services in one process. Compared with plain JavaScript, TypeScript catches mismatches in internal expense, split-session, and API types at build time, while the app validates untrusted request data at runtime. |
| Express 5.2.1 | Express handles routing, middleware, bounded JSON parsing, and errors. Compared with Node’s raw HTTP module, it lets Ledger apply shared session and request-handling middleware across feature routes without implementing routing and middleware dispatch itself. |
| escape-html ^1.0.3 | escape-html escapes the group name, inviter name and invitation token in the public invitation page (`GET /invite/{token}`), the only HTML the backend renders. Compared with a template engine, one small escaping function is enough for a single page, and compared with hand-written escaping it covers every HTML special character. |
| Mongoose ^9.11.2 | Mongoose defines MongoDB schemas and indexes for groups, expenses, and split sessions and supports conditional updates and aggregation. Compared with using the MongoDB driver directly, it keeps document definitions and validation close to the models while still allowing database-level updates for operations such as exclusive item claims. Its `sanitizeFilter` option, together with explicit validation of every identifier, keeps client input from becoming MongoDB query operators. This replaced the separate mongo-sanitize package, which only stripped operators and could not check that an identifier was well formed. |
| google-auth-library 11.1.0 | The backend verifies Google ID-token signatures, audience, issuer, and expiry with this library. Compared with implementing Google token verification from scratch, the library handles Google’s signing keys and token checks while Ledger remains responsible for issuing its own sessions. |
| Node crypto | Node crypto supplies scrypt password hashing with salts, secure random session and invitation tokens, and SHA-256 token hashes. Its built-in primitives cover these needs without adding separate hashing and token-generation packages. |
| pdfjs-dist 6.4.299 | PDF.js extracts text from supported bank-statement PDFs on the backend. Compared with routing text PDFs through OCR or AI recognition, reading the existing text layer keeps statement parsing independent of the receipt-recognition provider. |
| Socket.IO 4.8.3 and Android client 2.1.2 | Socket.IO delivers authenticated live split updates over `/dutch`, with WSS in release. Compared with periodic polling alone, it can push accepted changes to connected members as they happen. Compared with raw WebSocket, it supplies namespaces, events, and client reconnection. Ledger handles recovery of missed state with snapshots. |
| dotenv | dotenv loads backend settings from a local `.env` file into environment variables. Compared with hard-coding values or maintaining a separate development configuration format, it lets local development and deployment use the same setting names, with secrets supplied outside application code. |
| Jest, Supertest, mongodb-memory-server | Jest runs domain and interface tests, Supertest sends requests through the Express routes, and mongodb-memory-server provides isolated MongoDB instances. Compared with mock-only tests, this setup exercises MongoDB-specific behavior such as unique indexes and conditional updates without relying on a shared database. |
| JUnit, Compose UI testing, Espresso | JUnit runs Android domain and persistence tests. Compose UI testing makes assertions against the same semantics users interact with, and Espresso supports device interactions such as Back navigation. Compared with coordinate-based UI scripts, these tests can target UI meaning and observable behavior even when the layout changes. |

### 3.8. Design of Non-Functional Requirements

#### NFR-1 — Financial Integrity
Shared expenses use integer-cent arithmetic and backend validation to ensure all splits equal the total. Deterministic rounding handles remainder cents. Unique request IDs prevent duplicate creation, while revision checks protect edits and deletions.

Personal records use minor-unit arithmetic and decimal FX conversion. Request fingerprints prevent inconsistent retries, and SQLite transactions save imported records and request results atomically. FX validation, field validation, and duplicate acknowledgement complete before saving.

Split sessions enforce exclusive item ownership through version checks. Operation keys make retries safe, and interrupted finalization resumes without creating another expense. Finalized expenses cannot be edited or deleted.

#### NFR-2 — Access Control and Privacy

Protected APIs and live connections validate session credentials and expiry. Group operations require active membership; owner actions and expense changes enforce role permissions. Members can retrieve only their own personal-entry share and operation results. Live delivery rechecks session and membership, immediately excluding removed members.

Personal records are stored locally in SQLite. Recognition requires explicit submission and validates upload size/type; the OpenAI key remains server-side, and uploaded documents are not persisted. CSV parsing runs on-device, while supported text PDFs can be parsed on the backend without external AI.

Paid recognition requires sign-in and applies rate and concurrency limits; per-account quotas remain planned. Guest FX, metadata, and text-PDF routes are rate-limited. Release connections require HTTPS/WSS.

#### NFR-3 — Real-Time Responsiveness

Android uses background coroutines. Backend limits on uploads, import rows, extraction concurrency and timeouts bound the work done per request, and FX caching avoids repeating a rate lookup. Group summaries include totals for every expense but at most the 50 most recent expense cards, so the response and the page stay the same size however long a group has been in use.

Committed changes are pushed over /dutch as soon as they are saved. Sequence numbers, snapshots and operation lookup recover missed updates. The intervals below follow from the NFR-3 targets:

- **3-second snapshot poll while disconnected.** Once the network returns, the next poll is at most 3 seconds away, which leaves up to 2 seconds for the request itself within the 5-second recovery target.
- **Socket.IO reconnection back-off from 1 to 10 seconds.** The first retry is fast enough for a brief signal loss, and the 10-second cap limits each device to one attempt every 10 seconds while the server is down. Polling restores the screen in the meantime, so the back-off does not lengthen recovery.
- **15-second check while connected (every fifth poll).** It catches a lost final event or a membership change that no later event would reveal. Even at the 100-member limit this adds only about 7 snapshot requests per second per session (100 members / 15 seconds).
- **Limits of 100 members per group and 200 units per split session.** The backend rejects anything larger, so these are the load the NFR-3 targets are stated for.

The 1-second delivery and 5-second recovery targets have not yet been measured at that load.
